universal-features.def: Features found in every living thing: DNA as the genetic material, a nearly universal genetic code, ribosomes that make proteins, ATP as the energy carrier, a plasma membrane and core pathways such as glycolysis. They point to one shared ancestor of all life.

eukaryote-shared.def: Features found together in all eukaryotes and in no prokaryote: a nucleus, membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria, linear chromosomes, genes interrupted by introns that are spliced out, and a cytoskeleton. They point to one shared ancestor of all eukaryotes.

luca.def: The last universal common ancestor (LUCA): the most recent population of cells from which every organism alive today descends. It was not the first life; it already had DNA, the genetic code, ribosomes and ATP.

three-domains.def: The three largest groups of life: Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya. Bacteria and Archaea are prokaryotes; Eukarya are the eukaryotes. Archaea share more features with Eukarya (histones, a complex RNA polymerase) than with Bacteria.

conserved-genes.def: A gene whose sequence has changed very little over long spans of time, so its versions in distantly related organisms are still alike. Its product does a job so central that most changes lower fitness and are removed by natural selection.
